text:
maria: heads-up: new vuln report came in from OSS tracker — grpc, plus jwt lib chaining. tagging eng-security.

devsec-bot: [vuln-notification] CVE-2026-4219 (grpc-go) / CVE-2026-4220 (golang-jwt) published. severity: HIGH. Affected versions: google.golang.org/grpc < v1.62.0; github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 < v4.1.2.

josh: thanks. quick scan: we import grpc in inference-runtime and in the test harness. jwt is used by auth service (oauth flow).

olivia: can someone grep the repo for those module paths and list affected services? I can start a deps PR but want to confirm scope first.

kai: ran `go list -m all | grep "google.golang.org/grpc"` in infra/ and runtime/ — both return v1.60.3. auth-service shows jwt v4.0.0.

maria: ok, that means both runtime and auth are affected. severity note from bot: exploit can lead to unauthenticated RPC elevation under specific streaming scenarios (grpc) and token forging for certain key parsing flows (jwt).

josh: do we have mitigations? Can we pin a safe version?

olivia: upstream fixed grpc in v1.62.0 with a behavior change to stream header parsing. jwt fix in v4.1.2. Both are minor bumps. We should aim to pin immediately and run tests.

kai: suggested immediate action: 1) create branch update/grpc-jwt-2026-4219-4220 2) bump modules in go.mod 3) run unit + e2e matrix 4) canary deploy auth and runtime with traffic limits.

maria: agree. SRE will want a short deploy window. @sre_lead can you reserve a canary window tonight?

sre_lead: we have a maintenance slot 02:00-04:00 UTC. canary ok at 02:15 with 5% traffic. rollback plan?

josh: rollback is just revert PR + redeploy previous image tag. we keep old images around for 7 days.

olivia: sample go.mod diffs I'll include in the PR:```
require (
  google.golang.org/grpc v1.62.0
  github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 v4.1.2
)
// temporary replace for testing older CI if needed
// replace google.golang.org/grpc => google.golang.org/grpc v1.62.0
```

kai: also check transitive deps; grpc bump pulls new x/net, might affect net/http behavior in our proxy tests. add integration test for long-lived streaming.

maria: can we backport to last supported release branches? we still have v1.3.x for some enterprise customers pinned.

olivia: yes, will create two PRs: main and release/v1.3.x. grpc fix is source-compatible but need to run smoke tests. If any API behavior changed we must document in release notes.

devsec-bot: [ticket-created] SEC-2026-0421 created: triage + patching for CVE-2026-4219 & CVE-2026-4220. Link: https://redwood.security/SEC-2026-0421

josh: testing notes: run `make test-integration` with env TEST_STREAM=true and auth integration tests. We'll also run fuzz on jwt parsing for 24h in CI.

kai: FYI I repro'd the header-parsing failure with a crafted stream request locally using grpc v1.60.3. After bump to v1.62.0 the repro fails (i.e., fixed).

maria: good. who will own the PRs? olivia takes runtime & release backport? josh takes auth-service?

olivia: I can do runtime + backport. will open PRs and add reviewers from eng-runtime and eng-sre.

josh: I'll do auth-service and oauth proxy. plan to include token regression tests and regenerate containers.

sre_lead: when PRs are ready ping me in #eng-oncall for canary. also add deploy-checklist: health-check endpoint, increased logging for 30m, and abort conditions.

maria: timeline: PRs by EOD, CI green + integration by tomorrow morning, canary tonight (02:15 UTC), full rollout after canary 1hr stable.

kai: potential tricky item: net/http behavior change from x/net bump could affect our internal proxy header trimming. I'll add a quick smoke test in infra/proxy.

olivia: also adding a go.sum regeneration and `go mod tidy` in each PR to avoid CI surprises.

josh: security note: do not change signing keys or key rotation during deploy. keep keys stable. KMS audit already logging requests so we can trace.

maria: good call. we'll update SEC ticket with deploy steps, PR links, test results, and rollback steps.

devsec-bot: [reminder] Please attach CVE mitigations to SEC-2026-0421 and mark customer-impact if release branch backports are required.

olivia: PRs opened: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/458 and https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/459 (v1.3.x backport). added CI matrix and canary config.

josh: auth PR: https://github.com/redwood/auth-service/pull/212. includes jwt bump + new token parsing unit tests. CI: all green.

maria: great. @sre_lead please schedule canary. I'll update the incident tracker and notify sales for customers on pinned branches.

sre_lead: canary started at 02:15 UTC with 5% traffic. monitoring dashboards pinned.

kai: initial metrics: no increased error rate, latency stable. increased ad-hoc logging shows no parse exceptions.

olivia: after 30m of canary everything looks good. promoting to 25% then 100% over next hour.

josh: auth canary also stable. no token regressions.

maria: closing loop: SEC-2026-0421 updated with PR links, canary notes, CVE references, and postmortem planned to document the triage timeline. thanks all. :thumbsup:

devsec-bot: [auto-close] SEC-2026-0421 moved to status: mitigated (monitoring).
